title: Identifiable held-out routing with deterministic structural product-key addressing
question: Does a compositional operator descriptor restore held-out operator admission at fixed absolute budgets, and can StructMeans and PST improve that address without adding execution-time verifier information?
hypothesis: The failure in frontier 001 is primarily representational/admission: a deterministic operator descriptor indexed by product keys should admit unseen toggle signatures better than the learned candidate embedding, while StructMeans should reduce the kind search space and PST should improve final transition compatibility.

arms.name: learned_pkm
arms.intervention: existing verifier-trained learned candidate representation with product-key routing

arms.name: structural_pkm
arms.intervention: deterministic operator descriptor in the same factorized product-key index

arms.name: structural_pkm_structmeans
arms.intervention: deterministic descriptor product-key routing plus StructMeans operator-kind admission

arms.name: structural_pkm_structmeans_pst
arms.intervention: deterministic descriptor product-key routing plus StructMeans admission plus PST reranking

task_protocol.identifiability: retain only state/goal pairs for which exactly one candidate in the full library reaches the goal
task_protocol.evaluation_success: selected candidate is executable and reaches the goal
task_protocol.target_index: post-hoc only; never exposed to route()

rules: No verifier outcome enters evaluation routing.
No C5 or asymptotic claim from final shortlist size alone.
All internal exact address scoring is counted separately.
StructMeans is trained only on verified training transitions.
PST is trained only on verified training transitions.
Execution success is primary; exact target index is diagnostic.
SECA is excluded from this single-step admission experiment and remains a separate composition mechanism.

decision_rule.condition: Compare all four arms at every registered M and absolute budget using execution_success and admission/cost diagnostics.
decision_rule.licenses: a workload-specific comparison of routing interventions.
decision_rule.does_not_license: universal routing improvement, hardware speedup, or asymptotic sublinear addressing.

decision_rule.condition: If structural_pkm materially raises exact/behavioral admission relative to learned_pkm under the same budget, the compositional descriptor hypothesis is supported on this workload.
decision_rule.licenses: support for structural address representation on this synthetic operator family.

held_constant: three operator kinds: toggle, set1, set0
600 representation-training steps per seed/M learned-PKM cell
evaluation uses held-out toggle operators and unique-target state/goal pairs
no verifier outcome enters evaluation routing
StructMeans and PST use only verified training transitions
SECA is excluded from single-step routing comparison
